title: 2.1.31 Guard with &&
description: Write an if statement whose condition combines two checks with &&. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: book 2.1.8: 'Combining Conditions', Example 2.1.9: Both conditions must hold

steps.title: Declare two variables
steps.instructions: Create two number variables, for example, age and score, and give each a value.

steps.title: Guard with &&
steps.instructions: Write an if statement whose condition uses && to combine two comparison checks (one for each variable). Inside the if block, log a message that says both conditions are met.

requirements.title: && combines two real comparisons
requirements.description: if statement condition uses && to combine two identifier-based comparisons, not just any two values. Help: 2.1.29 (Logical Operators)

requirements.title: two variables declared
requirements.description: Two variables are declared and given values before the if, in any shape. Help: 2.1.29 (Logical Operators)

requirements.title: a message is printed inside the if block
requirements.description: console.log runs inside the if block, as step 2 asks. Help: 2.1.29 (Logical Operators)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "2.1.31 Guard with &&". The task they were given: Create two number variables, for example, age and score, and give each a value. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
